job.job_description:
Youve built projects. You know React basics. Youve deployed something to the internet. But you havent shipped code that thousands of users depend on - until now.

This is a full-time role. Well expect you to grow fast, learn in production, and take ownership. Well also give you people to learn from and space to develop into a solid engineer.

Youll be uncomfortable sometimes. Thats the point. Discomfort is where growth happens.

What You Will Do
Work inside a delivery pod with senior engineers, backend developers, product managers, and designers.
Build React components, manage state, and handle API integration.
Implement responsive designs that work across devices.
Participate in code reviews and sprint cycles.
Debug issues and ship fixes.
Take feedback, iterate, and improve.
What We Are Looking For
Strong React fundamentals: Hooks (useState, useEffect, useCallback), functional components, component lifecycle.
Comfort with modern JavaScript (ES6+): arrow functions, destructuring, promises, async/await.
HTML and CSS proficiency: flexbox, grid, responsive layouts.
Ability to fetch data from APIs and integrate it into React components.
Git basics: clone, commit, push, pull - comfortable working in teams.
A shipped project (internship, portfolio, hackathon, or deployed app showing real code).
Good to Have
Experience managing component state with Context API or a state library.
Understanding of responsive design and mobile-first principles.
Familiarity with browser DevTools (debugging, network tab, console errors).
Basic testing exposure (Jest or React Testing Library).
Experience with TailwindCSS, styled-components, or similar.
Deployed a React app (Vercel, Netlify, or GitHub Pages).
Familiarity with Figma or basic design tool understanding.
Knowledge of performance optimisation (lazy loading, code splitting).
Previous experience in a team environment with code reviews and feedback.
What You Will Work On
Week 1-2: Shadow code, understand our architecture, deploy a small feature.
Week 3-4: Own a component or small feature end-to-end.
Month 2: Start taking ownership of features with support.
Month 3+: Ship independently with code review.
Youll be paired with senior developers, given real problems, and reviewed at every step.
Why Kuvaka
Your first real job matters. You could join a consultancy and build 50 micro-features, or join Kuvaka and build real products - products that matter, that users depend on, that move businesses.
Youll work alongside engineers who care about code quality and shipping. Youll see what production-grade really means. Your code this week runs in production next week.
Youll see AI integration, cloud infrastructure, and modern product development. You wont be building CRUD apps - youll be building components of systems that solve real problems.
Growth is fast. If you ship and improve, that shows.
